tagline.text: An upscale BGC mall with a rooftop Skypark, Samsung Hall and IMAX under one roof

location.label: Location
location.text: Corner of 26th Street and McKinley Parkway, Bonifacio Global City (BGC), Taguig

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (an indoor stop that avoids the midday heat and rainy-season showers)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,500 (per person for meals, coffee, a movie and transport; shopping excluded)

children.text: SM Aura Premier is an SM Supermall that opened in BGC in May 2013 and has officially been called SM Aura since 2023. This eight-level mall, designed by Arquitectonica, combines a rooftop garden called the Skypark, the 1,000-seat Samsung Hall, an IMAX cinema and a food hall, making it a great place to rest during a BGC outing.

SM Aura Premier is a large shopping mall at the corner of 26th Street and McKinley Parkway in Bonifacio Global City (BGC), Taguig. It is owned and operated by SM Prime Holdings and opened on May 17, 2013. It is the 13th SM Supermall in Metro Manila and the 47th SM Prime mall overall. The name comes from the chemical symbols for gold (Au) and radium (Ra), and SM explains that it stands for luxury and elegance that emanates from within.

The mall's official name was "SM Aura Premier" for a long time. In 2023 SM tidied up the names of its Premier-branded malls, so it is now called "SM Aura," but map apps, review sites, taxi drivers and Korean community sites still widely use "Aura Premier." Both names lead to the same mall, so you can search for either one. This guide keeps "Premier" in the title because it is the name familiar to Korean travelers.
The building was designed by the architecture firm Arquitectonica with EDGE Interior Designers. According to Wikipedia, its floor area is about
200,000 square meters

, and its eight upper floors and three basement levels hold more than 300 stores and 8 anchor tenants. While many SM malls are wide, box-shaped buildings, Aura is known for a stepped structure with rooftop terraces on successive floors. From the 5th to the 7th floor the roof is landscaped as a garden, and this is the mall's signature Skypark. It is described as having al fresco bars and restaurants, sculptures, botanical gardens and a mini-golf course. Facilities can change, so check before you go.

Inside, the SM Store (department store) and SM Supermarket are the anchors, and tenants include Uniqlo, Stradivarius, Crate & Barrel, Ramen Nagi and Fitness First Platinum. The 4th floor has the upscale food hall Food on Four and the cinemas, and the 3rd and 4th floors house the convention center. Samsung Hall on the 6th floor is a 1,000-seat performance venue that opened in October 2013 and has hosted international bands. The 7th floor has the 250-seat Chapel of San Pedro Calungsod. For travelers, it is a base where you can cool off or shelter from the rain while walking around BGC, and take care of meals, movies and shopping in one place. The 29-story office building SM Aura Tower is attached to the mall, so there are many office workers on weekday afternoons, and some government offices and companies are based there. Wikipedia describes the mall as the first in the Philippines to receive LEED Gold certification. It underwent a major renovation in 2023; the Director's Club cinema reopened in January 2024 and the Food on Four food hall reopened with a new look in April 2024. Because stores and facilities change so often, check the official mall directory before you visit if you have a particular shop in mind.

A stepped rooftop garden on the 5th to 7th floors, with bars and restaurants that have outdoor seating among sculptures and botanical gardens. It is a nice place for a drink while looking at the BGC night view after dark, and it is also good for photos in the daytime. It is outdoors, so avoid it in the rain and at midday.

This 1,000-seat performance venue on the 6th floor opened on October 25, 2013. International bands and singers often perform here on tour, so if your schedule matches you can experience a local concert. Check the official announcements for performance schedules and tickets.

The 4th floor has regular cinemas, Director's Club theaters where you can order food to your seat (two or three, depending on the source), and an IMAX theater. The IMAX theater closed on June 28, 2024 for an upgrade to a laser system and is reported to have reopened on September 17, 2024. Check showtimes on SM Cinema.

This food hall on the 4th floor had about 18 specialty restaurants according to a 2023 guide, and it reopened after a makeover in April 2024. It feels more upscale than an ordinary food court, which makes it easy to pick a meal in one place. Prices vary by outlet.

The roof level on the 5th floor has a restaurant area called "Dine at the Fifth" where you can eat on a terrace. Reviews say there are many upscale restaurants, so it is worth considering for dinner or a get-together.
This 250-seat Catholic chapel on the 7th floor is named after the Filipino saint Pedro Calungsod and is known for its distinctive cave-like exterior. Check the Mass times locally, and visit quietly.
Stores such as Stuart Weitzman, Calvin Klein, Uniqlo, Stradivarius and Crate & Barrel are reported to be tenants. Brands change often, so check ahead for any shop you want to visit.
In BGC the sun is strong for walking and showers are frequent in the rainy season. The air-conditioned mall makes a good break between outdoor stops in BGC.

items.title: Half-day course
items.subtitle: Lunch, shopping and a stroll through the Skypark

children.text: Visit right after the mall opens and check the layout on the information desk or a mall map. Taking a photo of the map in the lobby is handy.
Have lunch at Food on Four on the 4th floor. With many restaurants to choose from, it works well for groups with different tastes.
Browse the SM Store and fashion shops, then pick up snacks such as sweets or coffee at the SM Supermarket.
Head up to the Skypark on the 5th to 7th floors and walk among the sculptures and gardens. If the sun is strong, rest at a shaded seat or a café.
Around sunset, have dinner at a Skypark restaurant and enjoy the lights of downtown BGC.

to
daily. Some reviews said the Skypark restaurants stay open later than the mall, but that is old information, so confirm locally.

items.title: Evening movie and concert course
items.subtitle: A finish to your BGC evening

children.text: After looking around BGC High Street or other streets, arrive at the mall by taxi or BGC Bus.
Have dinner. If you have a movie or concert afterward, allow plenty of time.
Watch a movie or a show at Samsung Hall. At the Director's Club theaters you can order food to your seat.
Call a Grab or taxi back to your hotel. If the queue at the mall's main entrance is long, try changing your pickup spot.
Concert nights draw crowds, so check tickets and times in advance and leave plenty of margin for your ride home.
From NAIA, the easiest way to reach BGC is by taxi or Grab. The trip can take
30 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes
or more depending on traffic, so avoid the rush hour (weekday evenings).
Fares vary a lot with time of day and traffic, so check in the app before booking or ask the driver to use the meter.

items.title: BGC Bus from Makati and EDSA

children.text: BGC Bus runs from EDSA Ayala and Market! Market! in Makati. A guide updated in January 2025 lists the fare on regular routes as about
, but a 2026 guide lists about
, so it seems to have changed; check when you board. Many routes run on weekdays from about 6 a.m. until night.

Wikipedia says the mall has a bus interchange served by BGC Bus routes AS02, AS10, C01, EX02, NR11 and WR12, plus city bus routes 15 and 16. Routes change often, so check the latest route map. Payment is often by Beep card, so it helps to buy one in advance at the terminals at Ayala or Market! Market! or at MRT stations.
The main drop-off is on the west side of the mall, and the taxi stand is on basement level 1 (on the east road side). When booking a Grab, set the pickup and drop-off point precisely on the map.
By car, you enter the parking area from Minipark Road, McKinley Parkway or the C-5 southbound service road. Parking is described as about
1,700 spaces
, but check the posted rates.
You can reach the mall on foot from central BGC, but the sun is strong during the day. Search for "SM Aura" in your map app.

It is an indoor mall, so the season hardly matters. Its value is greatest when it is too hot at midday or there is nowhere else to go in the rainy season. The Skypark is outdoors, so evenings in the dry season are the most pleasant.
Weekday daytimes are quiet, while weekend evenings and the December holiday season are crowded. BGC roads also jam at rush hour, so allow plenty of travel time.

BGC is a new town full of hotels and serviced residences, so it is easy to find a place to stay near the mall. Room rates vary greatly with season and exchange rate, so check by date on a booking site. You can travel between Makati and BGC by taxi, so choose accommodation to fit your route.

You can take care of all your meals inside the mall. Food on Four on the 4th floor is good for comparing several restaurants, and the 5th-floor restaurants and the Skypark suit an evening mood. Japanese chains such as Ramen Nagi and places such as The Food Hall (formerly Todd English Food Hall) are also mentioned. Tenants change often, so confirm locally that a place you want to visit is open. Cards are accepted at most places, but it is handy to carry a little cash too.
The official hours are listed as
to
daily. They may differ on holidays and at year end, so check just before you go.
In map apps, both "SM Aura" and "SM Aura Premier" lead to the same mall.
The mall is strongly air-conditioned, so bring a light jacket.
There are bag checks at the entrances, so follow staff instructions.
Check showtimes on SM Cinema and book popular films in advance.
The Skypark is outdoors, so avoiding midday heat and rain and going around sunset is most pleasant.
When calling a Grab, specify the pickup spot precisely, and leave extra time at rush hour.
The mall is large with many floors and it is easy to get lost, so take a photo of the floor directory when you arrive.
The mall gets crowded on concert nights, so check the schedule first.
Opening hours, cinema and Skypark facility operations and the tenant lineup change often, so check the latest announcements on the official channels just before you visit.
In crowded places, watch out for pickpockets and lost phones.
Ask taxi drivers to use the meter, and consider Grab if you have a lot of luggage.
BGC Bus routes and fares may change, so check the latest information before boarding.
The Skypark is outdoors, so be prepared for rain and strong sun.
In an emergency or earthquake, follow staff instructions and the emergency exit signs.
The new town where the mall stands is good for strolling past cafés and street art. Many places are within walking distance of the mall.
It takes about
20–40 minutes
by Grab or taxi, depending on traffic.
Another SM mall on the Ortigas side, reachable by taxi or Grab.
A business district north of BGC that is easy to combine into the same day's plan.
